newsitem.title: USA: Accord reported on Mexicop-drugs legislation.
newsitem.headline: Accord reported on Mexicop-drugs legislation.

text.p: U.S. Senate negotiators and the Clinton administration reached agreement late on Wednesday on legislation calling on Mexico to crack down on illegal drugs, a Senate source said.
The 11th-hour agreement followed further concessions by senators to accommodate administration concerns, the source said. There was no immediate comment from the administration.

A major sticking point for the administration had been a provision under which Congress would vote in September on whether Mexico had made an adequate response to demands for stepped up anti-drug efforts. Under the agreement this provision was eliminated.

The agreement apparently cleared the way for Senate debate on the legislation on Thursday, although this would require that Democrats relax a threat to block all legislation in an attempt to force Republicans to set a date for consideration of a chemical weapons treaty.

Without an accord on compromise drugs legislation, the Senate would have been faced with a debate and vote on a measure overturning President Bill Clinton's certification that Mexico is fully cooperating in the anti-drug war.
